newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Voting begins in Romanian general election.
newsitem.headline: Voting begins in Romanian general election.

text.p: Polling stations across Romania opened early on Sunday with voters choosing a president and parliament in the Balkan country's third post-communist elections.

Romania, the only East European country where the opposition has yet to rule, will either re-elect the ex-communists who have ruled since 1989 and who promise stability or centrist reformers offering economic reform.
State radio said that all 15,117 polling stations in 42 regions opened at 6 a.m. (0400 GMT). They are due to close at 9 p.m. (1900 GMT) or midnight if there is a late surge of voters.
In Bucharest elderly women strolled through the cool dawn air to vote early and avoid the rush expected later in the day.

Some 17 million people are eligible to vote and turnout is expected to be 70 percent. As well as electing a president, voters decide who fills 341 seats in the lower Chamber of Deputies and 143 seats in the upper house, the Senate.
The incumbent President Ion Iliescu, a veteran communist in power since the execution of Stalinist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu in December 1989, hopes voters will keep him in office for a new term.

Iliescu, favoured in opinion polls, is likely to face a second round run-off with one of his main rivals -- academic Emil Constantinescu or reformist ex-premier Petre Roman -- who have gained ground over the two-month campaign.
If Iliescu wins he may face a hostile coalition government.
His Party of Social Democracy is mired in corruption scandals and running behind Constantinescu's Democratic Convention (CDR) bloc.
